findings.issue_text: [High/security] GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() checks both VIEW and MANAGE, allowing callers with only realm-wide Groups VIEW permission to pass requireManage() and perform group mutations

[High/bug] GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses the authorization resource UUID from groupResource.getId() instead of the group ID stored in groupResource.getName(), causing per-group permissions to be evaluated against the wrong resource and incorrect filtering of user searches and counts

goldens.comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: [High/bug] GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() uses the authorization resource UUID from groupResource.getId() instead of the group ID stored in groupResource.getName(), causing per-group permissions to be evaluated against the wrong resource and incorrect filtering of user searches and counts
per_golden_matches.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same problem as the golden comment: in getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), the code uses groupResource.getId() (the authorization resource UUID) when it should be using groupResource.getName() (the actual group ID). Both comments point out that this mismatch causes per-group permissions to be evaluated incorrectly, affecting user filtering and counts. The candidate correctly identifies the root cause (getId() vs getName()) and the consequences (wrong resource evaluation, incorrect filtering).
